q: In which direction are protons pumped during electron transport, and what makes the gradient steep?
options: Matrix → intermembrane space; the small volume there lets H+ concentration rise quickly
From the intermembrane space into the matrix; the large matrix volume holds many more protons
From the cytoplasm into the matrix, through channels in the outer mitochondrial membrane
From the matrix out into the cytoplasm, by flowing through the ATP synthase complex
explanation: Complexes I, III and IV use energy from electron flow to pump H+ across the inner membrane, from the matrix into the intermembrane space. Because that space is so narrow, relatively few protons create a large concentration (and charge) difference. The inner membrane is impermeable to H+, so the gradient is maintained until protons flow back through ATP synthase.
